why: A clockwise quarter turn sends (r, c) to (c, n-1-r). That equals a transpose (swap (r, c) with (c, r)) followed by reversing every row, and both can be done in place.
hints: Write where cell (r, c) goes after a clockwise rotation.
(r, c) -> (c, n-1-r) splits into two easy in-place moves: transpose, then mirror each row left to right.
Swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for j > i only, then reverse each row. O(n^2) time, O(1) extra space.
pitfalls: Transposing over all (i, j) instead of j > i swaps each pair twice and undoes itself.
Reversing the row order instead of each row gives a counter-clockwise turn.
